508.h: The University of Cross River State (UNICROSS), formerly Cross River University of Technology (CRUTECH), is a public university owned by the Cross River State Government. Governor Donald Duke created it in 2002 by merging three state institutions: the Polytechnic of Calabar, the College of Education and the Ibrahim Babangida College of Agriculture. The National Universities Commission records 2004. In February 2021 a law approved by Governor Benedict Ayade renamed it, so that it could operate as a conventional university offering more professional courses, rather than a university of technology.
508.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate degree courses.
508.c: It has four campuses in four local government areas of Cross River State, with its main base in Calabar.

380.h: The Federal University of Education, Pankshin was founded in 1974 as the Federal Advanced Teachers College, later renamed Federal College of Education, Pankshin, whose degree programmes were run in affiliation with the University of Jos. On 23 September 2024 it was upgraded to a federal university of education, with a mandate to produce graduate teachers to international standards and to become a centre of research in education.
380.a: The university is organised into colleges that include a College of Adult, Non-Formal and Special Needs Education, which trains teachers for adult and continuing education and for learners with special needs, and a College of Arts and Social Sciences, which covers subjects such as religious studies.
380.c: It is located in Pankshin, Plateau State.

404.h: Legacy University, Okija is a private university, one of the private universities approved by the Federal Government in 2016. On 22 November 2019 it received accreditation for all its programmes from the National Universities Commission. At a later accreditation visit in December 2024 its economics programme scored 92 per cent and gained full accreditation.
404.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes, including economics and other social sciences.
404.c: It is located at Okija, in Ihiala local government area of Anambra State.

500.h: Aliko Dangote University of Science and Technology, formerly Kano University of Science and Technology (KUST), is a public university owned by the Kano State Government. It was proposed by Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso during his first term as governor, and the National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2000; teaching began in 2001. In 2022 Governor Abdullahi Umar Ganduje renamed it after the industrialist Aliko Dangote.
500.a: The university focuses on science and technology programmes and is a member of the Association of Commonwealth Universities. Its library was established in 2001, with circulation, reference, serials and e-library units.
500.c: It is located in Wudil, Kano State.

475.h: The Nigerian University of Technology and Management (NUTM) is a private university founded in 2019 to develop leaders in technology and management. Its first programme, launched in 2020, was the NUTM Scholars Programme, a one-year interdisciplinary postgraduate course in technology, entrepreneurship and design, which ran until 2024. Its pioneer vice-chancellor was the engineer Aderemi Aaron-Anthony Atayero. The National Universities Commission records its licence in 2023.
475.a: NUTM provides education in science, technology, engineering, mathematics and management at undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral levels.
475.c: The university first operated from Landmark Boulevard in Lagos and then moved to a temporary site in Apapa. A permanent campus is planned in Ogun State.

360.h: The Federal University of Agriculture, Zuru (FUAZ) began as the College of Agriculture, Zuru, which was affiliated to Ahmadu Bello University and came under the National Board for Technical Education in 1977. A bill sponsored by Senator Bala Ibn Na'Allah to upgrade it to a university passed the Senate in April 2019, and the university began full operations in September 2020. President Muhammadu Buhari appointed Professor Musa Isiyaku Ahmed as its pioneer vice-chancellor.
360.a: FUAZ is organised into a College of Agriculture, a College of Science and a College of Veterinary Medicine.
360.c: It is located in Zuru, Kebbi State.

435.h: Nigerian British University (NBU) is a private, co-educational university owned and run by the Adorable Foundation for Educational Development, which set it up to bring technology-driven teaching and learning to Nigeria. The National Universities Commission approved it in April 2022, and it was formally commissioned by Abia State governor Okezie Ikpeazu in February 2023, who awarded scholarships to its first twenty students. The university has a strict policy against cultism, drug abuse and other anti-social behaviour.
435.c: It is located in Asa, Abia State.

447.h: Amadeus University is a private university, one of 37 new private universities licensed by the National Universities Commission in 2023. The Commission cleared its resource verification in June 2023, and teaching began on 28 October 2024. It offered scholarships to some members of its pioneer class.
447.a: The university was approved to run 19 undergraduate degree programmes in faculties of Allied Health Sciences, Engineering, Science and Computing, and Social and Management Sciences. Its engineering courses are approved by the Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN), and law, medicine and surgery, and pharmacy were approved to start in the 2025/2026 session.
447.c: It is located in the Amizi community of Ikwuano local government area, Abia State.

418.h: Mudiame University is a private university founded by Professor Sunny Eromosele Eboh, chief executive of Mudiame International Limited and the Mudiame Welding Institute. The Federal Executive Council licensed it in 2021, and it graduated its first students, from the 2021/2022 intake, in 2025. In 2023 it took second place nationally in a technology and innovation competition for work on 'aqua-diesel' fuel.
418.a: The university has four main academic divisions: a College of Medicine, a School of Basic Medical Sciences, a School of Engineering and Technology, and a School of Science and Information Technology, together with a school of entrepreneurship.
418.c: It is located in Irrua, Edo State.

467.h: Miva Open University is a private online university established on 10 March 2023 by the uLesson Group, a Nigerian education technology company that also operates in four other West African countries. It received its licence from the National Universities Commission on 15 May 2023 and began admitting students on 25 May 2023, initially offering eight disciplines in two faculties.
467.a: Courses now include computer science, cyber security, data science, software engineering, information technology, public health, nursing science, accounting, economics, entrepreneurship, criminology and security studies, mass communication, business management, and public policy and administration, as well as an MBA. Students study online rather than on a campus, which suits working adults and learners outside the major cities.
467.c: Its primary base is in Abuja.

406.h: Coal City University (CCU) is a private, non-profit, co-educational university established in 2016. It takes its name from Enugu's nickname, the Coal City, which comes from the coal mining that shaped the city's history. It is recognised by the National Universities Commission, which gave full accreditation to its social science and political science programmes in December 2024 with a score of 84.4 per cent.
406.a: The university has faculties of Natural and Applied Sciences; Education; and Arts, Social and Management Sciences. Courses include accounting, biochemistry, biology, business administration, business education, chemistry, computer science, and criminology and security studies.
406.c: Its two campuses, at Emene and Independence Layout in Enugu, cover about 432 acres in all.
